advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix store_copy_entries stride so limit<len(canonical)<2*limit still spans the whole history (e.g. use a fractional/index-based stride) and add a boundary test.
evidence: tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py:67-69: `if limit > 0 and len(canonical) > limit:` / `stride = len(canonical) // limit` / `canonical = canonical[::stride][:limit]`
With len(canonical)=201 and limit=200: stride = 201//200 = 1, canonical[::1][:200] == canonical[:200] — the first 200 (oldest) ids, a contiguous era, not a span
Docstring claims: 'Canonical-id tickets are sampled at an even stride so the slice spans the store's whole history instead of one contiguous era'
test_the_slice_spans_the_whole_store_rather_than_one_contiguous_era only tests 1000 names against limit=10 (100x ratio), never the limit<len<2*limit boundary where the head-slice bug manifests
advisory.finding: store_copy_entries produces a contiguous HEAD slice instead of an evenly-strided sample whenever limit < len(canonical) < 2*limit. stride = len(canonical)//limit evaluates to 1 in that range, so canonical[::1][:limit] returns the first `limit` ids — the oldest tickets only — silently defeating the documented 'slice spans the store's whole history rather than one contiguous era' guarantee.
scenarios: A store whose canonical-ticket count sits between STORE_COPY_TICKET_LIMIT (200) and 400 — the rehearsal silently narrows to the oldest tickets
advisory.suggested_fix: Select by evenly spaced indices rather than integer-floor stride, e.g. `idx = [round(i * (len(canonical) - 1) / (limit - 1)) for i in range(limit)]; canonical = [canonical[j] for j in idx]` (or use a float step), so the last selected id is always near the newest ticket regardless of the ratio.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Drain git archive's stderr concurrently (e.g. via a thread or by reading it before wait()) to avoid a full-pipe deadlock in extract_store_snapshot.
evidence: tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py:83-84: `stdout=subprocess.PIPE,` / `stderr=subprocess.PIPE,` on the git archive Popen
tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py:106-107: `archive.wait()` then `failure = (archive.stderr.read() ...)` — stderr is read only AFTER wait() returns
During the transfer only tar's stdout/stderr are drained via extract.communicate(); git's stderr is never read until git has already exited
dropped.finding: In extract_store_snapshot, git archive's stderr is a PIPE that is not drained until after tar's communicate() and archive.wait(). If git writes enough to fill the stderr pipe buffer (~64 KB) while tar is still consuming stdout, git blocks on the stderr write and archive.wait() can hang, deadlocking the fixture.
scenarios: git archive emitting a large volume of warnings/progress to stderr on a big or malformed tree while tar is still reading stdout
